claims.text: Hadrian's Gate, known in Turkish as Üçkapılar meaning 'The Three Gates', is a Roman triumphal arch built in honour of the Emperor Hadrian, who visited the city in 130 CE.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: Standing about 8 meters high, the gate is considered to be Pamphylia's most beautiful gate and is built almost entirely of white marble, except for the granite pillars.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: The three passageways are decorated with floral and rosette reliefs, and a frieze of floral motifs with lion heads runs across the entablature above.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: The original gate was two stories, and although little is known of the top story, it is believed to have held statues of the emperor and his family.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: The gate was rediscovered by the Irish hydrographer Francis Beaufort in 1817, while commanding on HMS Fridericksteen.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: According to local legend, Sultana Belkis, the Queen of Sheba, is said to have passed under those gates on her way to visit King Solomon.
claims.subject: self
